summary.text: The Giza pyramid complex in Egypt is home to the Great Pyramid, the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure, their associated complexes and the Great Sphinx.
All were built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom, between about 2600 and 2500 BC.
The site also includes temples, cemeteries and the remains of a workers' village, at the edge of the Western Desert near Cairo.

facts.label: Great Pyramid built
facts.value: Also called Khufu's pyramid; c. 2580 to c. 2560 BC

facts.label: Distance from Cairo
facts.value: About 13 km southwest of the city centre

facts.label: Seven Wonders status
facts.value: Oldest Wonder and the only one still standing

items.prompt: Standing at Giza, one pyramid looks bigger than its neighbour built for Khufu. Why is that look misleading?

options.label: It stands on higher ground and is steeper
It is made of much larger limestone blocks
It has far more casing stone covering it
It was built much later and so is taller

items.explain: Khafre's pyramid sits higher and rises at a steeper angle, but it is in fact smaller in both height and volume.

items.prompt: Of the ancient world's Seven Wonders, only one can still be visited. Which?
items.explain: The Great Pyramid was listed as a Wonder and is the oldest of them and the only one still in existence.

items.prompt: Egyptologists broadly agree on whose face the Great Sphinx carries. Whose?

options.label: Khufu, whose pyramid is the Great Pyramid
Menkaure, whose pyramid is the smallest
Antipater, who listed the Seven Wonders
Khafre, whose pyramid sits near the Sphinx

items.explain: The consensus is that the Sphinx's head is Khafre's, and a Sphinx temple is part of Khafre's complex.

items.prompt: Builders at Giza needed vast amounts of limestone. Where did most of it come from?

options.label: Quarries at Tura, across the river
The rock formation under the site itself

items.explain: Most of the limestone originates from the underlying Mokattam Formation; the fine white casing stones came from Tura.

items.prompt: Three pits were cut beside the Great Pyramid. What did the two on its south side hold when they were excavated?
items.explain: The boat pits contained a ship, and the two on the south side held intact ships when excavated.

items.prompt: Khufu's pyramid once had a smooth outer layer, and a few pieces remain at its base. What were those casing stones made of?

options.label: Dark basalt from the temple floors

items.explain: The remaining casing stones were fine white limestone quarried at Tura.

paragraphs.heading: Three pyramids and a Sphinx
paragraphs.text: The Great Pyramid was built around 2580 to 2560 BC. A few hundred metres to its south-west stands Khafre's slightly smaller pyramid, and a few hundred metres farther on is the fairly modest pyramid of Menkaure. Khafre's pyramid can seem larger than Khufu's, since it sits on higher ground and its sides slope more steeply, yet it is smaller in both height and volume. On the eastern side of the site sits the Great Sphinx; it dates from Khafre's reign, and Egyptologists agree its head is his. Smaller satellite pyramids, known as queens' pyramids, along with causeways and temples, complete the scene.

paragraphs.heading: A pyramid and its temples
paragraphs.text: Khufu's pyramid was joined to a chain of other buildings. The chain began with a valley temple, now buried under the village of Nazlet el-Samman, from which a causeway led to a mortuary temple joined to the pyramid. Three small queens' pyramids and three boat pits belong to it too. The two pits on the south side held intact ships when they were excavated, and one of them, the Khufu ship, has been restored and moved to the Grand Egyptian Museum. Khafre's complex had a valley temple and a causeway too, plus a mortuary temple, the pyramid itself and a temple for the Sphinx.

paragraphs.heading: Menkaure's smaller complex
paragraphs.text: Menkaure's complex had four main parts: a valley temple, a causeway, a mortuary temple and his pyramid. Both temples held several statues of the king. In the 5th Dynasty a smaller ante-temple was added to the valley temple. His pyramid was finished around 2510 BC and has three smaller queens' pyramids of its own.

paragraphs.heading: The stone they used
paragraphs.text: Most of the limestone in the pyramids came from the Mokattam Formation, the rock layer beneath the site. Khufu's pyramid still keeps a few casing stones at its base, made of fine white limestone quarried at Tura. Khafre's pyramid still shows plenty of casing stones near its peak. Of the four major monuments, only Menkaure's pyramid has lost all of its original polished limestone casing.

paragraphs.heading: The last ancient Wonder
paragraphs.text: The Great Pyramid and Khafre's pyramid are the largest pyramids built in ancient Egypt, and in the West they have long served as symbols of Ancient Egypt. Their fame grew in Hellenistic times, when Antipater of Sidon named the Great Pyramid as one of the Seven Wonders of the World. Of those Wonders it is by far the oldest, and the only one still standing.

paragraphs.heading: People before the pyramids
paragraphs.text: The Giza plateau was lived on before any pyramid rose there. At the foot of the Great Pyramid, diggers found four jars of the Maadi culture, probably from an earlier settlement that had been disturbed. A new look at radiocarbon dates puts the settlement that gave the Maadi culture its name at about 3800 to 3400 BC, which is likely the widest possible range for the Giza remains too.
